translations.text: i.e. this is apostolic authority, then: to place his own name at the beginning of the epistle.
i.e. it was the will of the Father that I should come.
i.e. Timothy was a preceptor and teacher to them, and a brother in the faith; it would not be unfitting even if it were in the flesh.
i.e. to the holy congregation that is in Corinth.
i.e. it is not only the people of Corinth to whom I wish this good, but I wish it to all the saints who are in Achaia.
i.e. 'we pray, I and Timothy, manifoldly': this is what is to be supplied [?].
i.e. in the same way.
i.e. besides the Father.
i.e. both the tribulations of the present world and future punishments.
i.e. through preaching to them; or, our freedom is an example of consolation and freedom to everyone.
from the [?].
i.e. so that we may strengthen everyone in the enduring of tribulations, as God strengthens us.
i.e. even we.

i.e. as great as the tribulation that is brought upon us, so great is the consolation that is brought. God therefore does not bring upon us tribulation that we cannot bear; whatever tribulation we endure, he gives consolation in return for it.
i.e. which comes upon us.
i.e. for our enduring of tribulations is consolation and salvation for you; i.e. what our master does, it is best for us to do.
i.e. through enduring the tribulations the salvation will come.
i.e. we have known that your faith will be firm in the tribulations.
i.e. I am glad that you should know it.
i.e. the great.
i.e. a burden of tribulations was laid upon us which strength could not bear.
i.e. which befell us.
i.e. it was wearisome to us to be alive, so that we longed with all desire to die.
i.e. because it had come near to death.

i.e. to preach the death of Christ; or, we are ready for death for Christ; or, the knowledge of tidings from death. Otherwise: we were weary of living. Question: what did we do? Not difficult: but the answer of death, etc., i.e. praying and wishing for our death is what we did, but we did not find it.
i.e. trust in ourselves, i.e. in our own prudence
i.e. his help will still be with us
i.e. your [?] (helping/supporting)
i.e. pray to God with us that we may endure our tribulations
i.e. your help indeed, so that from many [persons] etc.
i.e. [people] will believe through us [?]
i.e. thanks are given
i.e. so that they may [?]
i.e. the salvation of multitudes through preaching, after we have been delivered
i.e. it is not false of us, against our conscience: it is not for reward or payment that we preach the gospel
in simplicity, i.e. not for reward or payment for ourselves, but it is for gathering multitudes into glory with God; we glory in sufferings; we do not preach for the sake of gain
i.e. this is God's simplicity: preaching the gospel without reward, without payment
i.e. so that reward and glory may be obtained for that
i.e. you know my conduct toward you, i.e. that I do not seek reward for my preaching
i.e. I am certain of it
i.e. to the end of perfection
i.e. a part of you, or a part of our teaching
i.e. it is through us that the glory will be yours in the future
i.e. since it is through your being brought to faith that we shall have glory in the day of our Lord
i.e. because I praise you and boast of you
i.e. penance. Question: what is the first grace? It is not hard to say: the forgiveness of sin through baptism. This is the second grace: the forgiveness of sin through penance.
i.e. [?] me, i.e. every way he went here, it is for preaching and teaching
i.e. for it is the habit of fickleness that what is said and what is done are different
i.e. for in what is thought according to the flesh there are usually falsehood and truth; my thinking, then, is not according to the flesh, but according to God, and there is no falsehood in him
i.e. that there should be, i.e. that my speech should be twofold, i.e. falsehood and truth, i.e. that what I would say with my lips and what I would think in my heart should be different
This is a kind of oath; or it may be a comparison, i.e. just as there are not two things in this, i.e. truth and falsehood, but only truth is in it, so it is truth that is in us.
i.e. it is truth alone that is in us.
i.e. who has been preached to you.
i.e. falsehood and truth at the same time.
i.e. *est*, i.e. truth.
i.e. it would be a strange thing for us to speak falsehood, for he who speaks in us, i.e. Jesus Christ, is truthful.
i.e. it is I myself who say it first.
i.e. in Jesus Christ there was not *est et non*, i.e. truth and falsehood; only *est* was there, i.e. truth, i.e. it will be a proof of truth.
i.e. the truth, i.e. what God promised has been fulfilled in Christ.
i.e. *Iesum*, i.e. it is through him that the grace of miracles and teaching has been given to us.
[?] the glory to us [?] [?]preach[?] [?] there is not, but [?] in him.
i.e. it is he who strengthens us along with you.
i.e. by the Holy Spirit.
i.e. it is he, God [?], i.e. in likeness to him in deeds and in morals.

i.e. he has given a pledge, i.e. a pledge that is worth [?] when he says [?] [?] the debt, eternal life and the heavenly kingdom, through [?] the pledge will be [?] the debt with us [?] Christ and the Holy Spirit.
i.e. this is an oath on my part.
i.e. it is out of mercy toward you that I did not come to you at once to bring punishment and reproof upon you, though I could have done that [?], as Peter [did to] Ananias and Sapphira.
i.e. we do not have power over your faith.
i.e. we are helping you by bringing you the grace of the Spirit, so that this is what causes joy to you and to us.
i.e. this indeed is what has caused us joy: your being in the faith and the steadfastness with which you stand firm in it.
i.e. so that there might be no need of rebuke now: rebuke and the exposing of sin in the first epistle, forgiveness and consolation in the last.
i.e. he counts the coming of the epistle as his own coming.
i.e. *consilium*, i.e. so that I might not cause you sorrow on the second coming.
i.e. through rebuke for sin.
i.e. through rebuke from me.
i.e. the word or deed with which I rebuked you above
i.e. your being in sin
i.e. the tribulations that I suffered in Asia
i.e. it is from you
i.e. it would have been more fitting for me to have joy from you than sorrow
i.e. I am certain that my joy will be joy to you
i.e. for your joy is joy to me
i.e. though there were other troubles upon us, care for you was dearer to us
i.e. it is not to bring sorrow upon you [that I write] this
i.e. but love
i.e. so that you may know how great my love is
i.e. so that I may not count the sin against you all; or, so that I may give help to you, so that it may not be heavy upon you alone
i.e. it is many who have rebuked him
i.e. but rebuke was good; if he amends, [let there be] forgiveness; it is not good for you, then, [to be] without forgiveness after rebuke
i.e. from despair
i.e. lest despair of forgiveness should swallow him up, and you [lose] him [?]
i.e. show your love towards him
i.e. to see whether you fulfil what was preached to you in the Gospel, i.e. forgiveness for everyone
i.e. the one whom you forgive, I forgive too
i.e. what I forgive for your sake, it is Christ who forgives it along with me
i.e. it is in the person of Christ that I do that
i.e. so that we may not be deceived, i.e. through despair; for he is cunning in persuading to sin; once it is completed, he persuades to despair after its completion
i.e. [?] there, then, the door we spoke of above: whoever it is that preaches it, and whoever has it
i.e. a multitude there was ready to believe; but I did not stay with it, because Titus was not there waiting for me
i.e. here is shown how great Paul's love was for them, in that he did not stay preaching to the multitude, because he was so eager to learn news from the messenger who had gone to them
i.e. which he has made renowned [?]
i.e. because we have made known the knowledge of Christ to everyone
i.e. through knowledge of the faith
i.e. they do not smell the scent of faith through us, and yet it is preached to them all the same
i.e. so that it is the odour of life unto life, and so that it is the odour of death unto death
i.e. not everyone
i.e. we are not like the teachers who have sought you around us; we do not boast of it to him, but only so that they may not receive any other
i.e. we do not speak one thing with the heart and another with the mouth, i.e. we do not seek a reward for teaching
i.e. to us the teaching that we preach
i.e. it is Christ that we preach
i.e. shall we begin, i.e. shall we be at it, then, after you have known us from the beginning, so that you have not looked past us?
or is it that we have need?
i.e. whether letters should be carried from us to give testimony of us
i.e. we will commend ourselves, then, anyway, by ourselves
i.e. there is no need, moreover, of a letter from you, for we know it already
i.e. your faith bears testimony of us
i.e. what is in our heart, you fulfil it
i.e. everyone knows us through your faith, i.e. it bears testimony, because you have believed
i.e. because you fulfil the commandment of Christ, while Christ is in your hearts
i.e. with ink
i.e. on the tablet of the heart
i.e. saying that you have been written by the Spirit in unity with Christ
i.e. it is not from ourselves that we are sufficient
i.e. so that we are sufficient for the preaching and teaching of everyone
i.e. [?] with him, that we receive sufficiency; or, it is he who has caused it

i.e. in that it punishes sin in everyone, and there is punishment in the future for transgression. That is why he says, 'the letter kills', because what it contained was 'let him die the death' (morte moriatur).
i.e. vengeance.
i.e. what Moses said used to be done; or, glory was shown at the giving of the Law.
i.e. what he says here is that honour should be shown to the preachers, i.e. that what they say should be fulfilled.
i.e. they could not bear to look at his face after he had been speaking with God when the Law was given to him.
i.e. because of its brightness.
i.e. this is what he is getting at from above, from 'quod si ministratio' (for if the ministration) etc.
i.e. the preachers of the New Testament: a great thing should be done for them.
i.e. of Moses.
i.e. the glory of the whole Old Law.
i.e. doing what the Law commands.
i.e. the glory of the whole New Testament.
i.e. in preaching.
i.e. to show that the children of Israel did not understand the mysteries, and that there was a veil of unbelief over their hearts.
i.e. the writing of this book.
i.e. in that they did not believe in Christ as he was prefigured in the mysteries of the Law.
i.e. 'nobis' (to us), i.e. there is no veil between us and Christ; or 'non revelatum est' (it is not revealed), i.e. to those Jews, i.e. they have not understood that 'in Christ' etc.
i.e. for the veil of the letter has been done away with through faith in Christ. Question: what was done for them? Not hard to answer: 'sed usque in hodiernum diem' (but even to this day) etc.
i.e. through faith in Christ.
i.e. they still do not understand the mystery of the Law, i.e. what has been foretold and prefigured about Christ.
i.e. etc.; or, all of them who will believe, [the?] twelve thousand of them [?] etc.; or, whoever of them believes will understand the mysteries of the Law.
i.e. as if he had said: the Jews pay attention only to what is carnal and to the literal history; not so [?] … the Lord is spiritual, and the whole New Testament is spiritual.
i.e. without being in servitude to the Law.
i.e. unveiled, i.e. we cast the veil off from us.
i.e. knowledge of the Godhead.
i.e. like Christ in conduct, or the image of the Transfiguration on Mount Tabor
i.e. as from the Spirit
i.e. the mercy of God that has brought about faith for us
i.e. curtailment
i.e. deceitfulness, as others who adulterate the Gospel
i.e. it is not for price or reward that we preach
i.e. in the manifestation
everyone's conscience knows our condition
i.e. if what we preach is obscure to anyone, it is not to anyone who fulfils it, but it is to someone who does not believe it
i.e. in which the glory of Christ is preached
i.e. the form of nature according to the divinity
i.e. this is why it is the glory of Christ that we preach: for we do not preach our own glory
it is for this reason indeed that we preach to you
i.e. the fire of the Holy Spirit, so that we may be knowledgeable in the mysteries of the Godhead
i.e. of knowledge, i.e. knowledge of the Godhead and the grace of the Spirit
we are not sorrowful
i.e. against great crushing [?]
i.e. we have not perished at all
i.e. because what we say is true
i.e. the cross; or, as Jesus was dead to this world, so also are we
i.e. which we endure
i.e. so that we may have the glory in which Christ is in heaven
i.e. the death to which we go brings about life for you, i.e. it is for the sake of your life that we go to death
i.e. it is for your sake
i.e. the variety of the gifts that are bestowed on everyone
i.e. of grace.
i.e. for the magnifying of God wholly [?]
i.e. better and better
i.e. its brevity
i.e. the great
i.e. a reward for us
i.e. let us not give love to the present things
i.e. the love of them is not worthy
i.e. it is right, however, to look upon these
i.e. the separation of body and soul is grievous to us
i.e. that a house of immortality from heaven might be granted around us
i.e. around the living one
i.e. in the body, or: the separation of body and soul is heavy to us
i.e. that life might come over that body
i.e. it is God
i.e. it is not knowledge for us
i.e. we have dared
i.e. we dare
i.e. we consent
i.e. it is easier for us to part from our body if what we have desired is fitting, i.e. to go in our body to heaven
i.e. since it is [?] , it is better for us to please him
i.e. it is pleasing to us, its good [?] from our body
i.e. works, i.e. faces are not shielded there when confessions are made on that day
i.e. he knows that we have fear of him
i.e. I am certain
i.e. that you too, then, may know us
i.e. we do not need you to look us over [?] at the beginning.
i.e. an occasion.
i.e. we leave it to you.
i.e. so that you do not let them get the upper hand over you.
i.e. in carnal things (in carnalibus), or 'it is judged' [?] (forbrethir).
i.e. so that it may be we whom you boast of, i.e. so that you may say: what they do for a master, we do not do it, though [?] you preach.
i.e. by charity (caritate), i.e. through contemplating God.
i.e. for you.
It is for you that it profits (proficit); it would be right for you, even if testimony were given about us [?].
i.e. to go beyond (excedere), or not to think on the desires and wishes of the world, but at one time we are meditating on God, at another time preaching; we do both out of love of God.
i.e. we are certain of it.
i.e. not from carnal desire (non desiderio carnali), i.e. so that no one should have any anxiety except to do the will of God.
i.e. that death is not counted as a disgrace, because he rose again.

i.e. since Christ has done all this for us, it is not right for anyone after that to live in carnal desire. Otherwise: we know of no one, that is, Christ, dying again for sinners (Aliter: neminem novimus Christum mori iterum pro peccatoribus).
i.e. Christ was in the flesh.
i.e. this is: he rose again and ascended (resurrexit et ascendit).
i.e. Godhead, i.e. it was not humanity without Godhead.
i.e. an embassy, as in: 'As the Father has sent me, so I also,' etc. (ut sicut misit me Pater et ego, etc.).
i.e. we do not plead by the power of the world, but for Christ's sake.
i.e. that one.

i.e. an offering. With them, 'sin' (peccatum) was the name for the offering that was offered for sin. He was offered, then, for the sin of the race of Adam, so it was fitting that he should be called 'sin' (peccatum).
i.e. a great abundance of the grace of God.
i.e. of the New Testament (novi testamenti), or the age of every person.
i.e. everyone's acceptance of faith, and everyone's acceptance by God.
i.e. the salvation of everyone through faith.
i.e. that we may not give it to anyone.
i.e. it is fitting for us that we should fulfil what we preach.
i.e. if we fulfil what we preach, we shall not be reproached afterwards.
i.e. in dangers.
i.e. of mind, or distress and hunger.
i.e. in blows.
i.e. in confinements.
i.e. going from territory to territory.
Sufferings under compulsion up to this point; sufferings of one's own will, this below.
i.e. in restraint, without [?].
i.e. in pleasantness.
i.e. without pretence, because the Holy Spirit flees what is feigned; so the Holy Spirit is in us.
i.e. not like the false apostles, on the lips only.
i.e. the working of miracles.
i.e. the weapons of righteousness for our protection.
i.e. so that pride may not seize us in prosperity, and despair may not seize us in adversity.
i.e. generis [?], i.e. whether we are praised or whether we are satirized, it does not give us pride, nor does it [?] upon us.
i.e. as though no one knew us, and yet he knows us; or unknown to men and known with God.
i.e. ready to go to death every day.
i.e. God protects us from every tribulation.
i.e. God protects us nevertheless.
i.e. we are joyful indeed nevertheless in tribulations.
i.e. in truth, or with the riches of the world.
i.e. spiritual mysteries, or food through our work, so that we may not be in hunger or in nakedness; as it is: the whole world belongs to the faithful man.
i.e., that we may not be in hunger [?] and nakedness [?] (nanocti [?])
i.e., we desire to preach doctrine to you.
i.e., the teaching that is offered to you is not narrow.
i.e., you, however, are narrow in receiving that teaching.
i.e., if you were good, there would be the reward that will be given to us.
i.e., as I have extended it, i.e., the teaching [?].
i.e., let your mind and your heart be broad in receiving this teaching.
i.e., let it not be the same yoke that you are in.
i.e., they are called a temple because it is the one God who dwells in them.
i.e., he gives them three names, then: temple of God, and sons, and dearest.
i.e., he joins himself with them, as is the custom of good teachers.
i.e., so that your body and your soul may be clean.
i.e., so that your soul may be holy in the fear of God.
i.e., we have deceived no one.
i.e., not because you have done this, i.e., injury, etc.
The praise of another is no reproach to anyone. Though I say this, you are not reproached; rather, it is for your instruction, so that you may do what we do and may not do what we do not do.
i.e., through fulfilling and imitating what we do.
i.e., I am fearless in giving testimony on your behalf.
i.e., because you act after our likeness, not in every manner, of true goodness.
i.e., because you are perfect, I feel no sorrow or trouble.
i.e., because we did not have news of you.
i.e., of heretics and others who are in fellowship and do not give their heart.
i.e., it is his custom to help every weak person in tribulations.
i.e., with news of you.
i.e., the joy that he had with you, i.e., because he found awaiting him desire and mourning and emulation.
i.e. tit [?]
i.e. your zeal against the other apostles on my behalf
i.e. though it be for an hour, i.e. a part of an hour
i.e. even if it were so [?], I did not regret it
i.e. this time
i.e. it is not your sorrow that causes joy to me
i.e. it is no loss to you, though it is not with you [?], for you are good already
i.e. that sorrow causes salvation
i.e. about the cares of the world, i.e. grief for anything that perishes, and for anything that is not obtained, and for anything that someone else has which you do not have
i.e. a great thing
i.e. certainly [?] of the will [?], i.e. good work after it
i.e. from care
i.e. it is for your consideration
i.e. you have done it, in that you prove yourselves to be chaste
i.e. he did not come back sorrowful
i.e. it was no disgrace to me to say to him that he would find joy with you and that you would be good in your conduct when he came to you
i.e. for our boasting
i.e. towards you [?]
i.e. the truth of everything, as I said
i.e. beyond everyone
i.e. he remembers
i.e. goodwill without stinginess
i.e. their poverty and their simplicity have brought about riches for us
i.e. it is that which I wonder at
i.e. it is from this that I bear witness to the strength of the love that was in them
i.e. the alms which is given by us to the saints; or, that they might have a share in ministering it.
i.e. for that alms.
i.e. it is clear, then, why Titus went, i.e. to seek alms.
i.e. you have all of them.
i.e. so that what you give may be better than anyone's.
i.e. to test your love.
i.e. it is fitting that you give something to his household; good are his [?] favours toward you.
i.e. by the work of God; this is my counsel: to give it.
i.e. because it is your desire.
i.e. from last year.
i.e. that willing.
i.e. the desire.
i.e. there is no need of payment or loan, but give what you have.
i.e. if it is with good will.
i.e. according to the means you have.
i.e. hunger, i.e. it is not right to feed the one party and to starve the other party.
i.e. the giving of the alms.
i.e. the abundance you have of the [?] riches.
i.e. so that they may pray to God for you.
i.e. so that no one may be defrauded by another.
i.e. his wealth was not more plentiful though he was strong at gathering.
i.e. his share was not less though he was weak at gathering.
i.e. in preaching the gospel, so that everyone praises him.
i.e. it is trustworthy in everyone's eyes that he should be at the [?] of their alms; or, it is fitting for him to be in the company of good men.
i.e. it is our desire, then, to do it for you.

i.e. by way of alms; or: in the belief that it was not for Jerusalem, i.e. the riches they would bring; or: the receiving of a reward for preaching — as I do not take it, so Luke does not take it either
i.e. preach the glory of God in all churches
i.e. so that every church may see it

i.e. two things, then, are understood in this testimony below: i.e. it would be [part of] the moral precept to all the Corinthians that I should not speak to them about the alms that is taken to Jerusalem, for I know that it is ready with you. Otherwise: it is concerning the alms that he enjoins above, but it is on the lay people that he enjoins their share; as for the people of [holy] orders and of perfect age, there is no need to enjoin them.
i.e. I am boasting on your behalf to the Macedonians
i.e. this is what I boast of
i.e. your summons had reached you before me [?]
i.e. so that my boasting may not be a shame to me
i.e. I am more anxious about the people outside, if they should know of it
i.e. so that it may not be a shame to you and to us
i.e. he gives the name of 'blessing' to that alms, since it is with blessing that it is bestowed
or circumventionem, i.e. deceit
i.e. when they enrich you [?]
if it is with contentment that they bestow it, we shall give thanks to God for it
i.e. through the thanksgiving of the saints when that alms is given
i.e. your confession is good
i.e. frequent is their prayer for you
i.e. I have believed that you will do it
i.e. through boldness of power
i.e. I have dared, i.e. vindicare [to avenge]
i.e. who have deserved it
i.e. so that we should come to avenge it [?]
i.e. first, of anything that is sent to you [?]
i.e. since he has boasted of power for himself up to now, he says now that he is a slave and not a lord

i.e. he says at first that he is a slave; he reflects again that he has done the works of a slave, i.e. so that no one should think that he is greater than slaves; and even when I have boasted, it was not for love of boasting, but so that there might be benefit to you through it, i.e. so that you might believe, and imitate my ways, and not believe anyone except someone who did these works
i.e. as though I could not [do] in person what I used to say through epistles [?]
i.e. the judgements that are written in the epistles are great
i.e. it is weak, however, when he is present
feeble, i.e. the speech is not eloquent, i.e. it is not firm, but it is simple and it is clear
i.e. as far as our word is able
i.e. we do not boast of what we shall not do after arriving; it is not mere stories for you [?]
i.e. our deed will be tested after arriving
i.e. we have not dared that
i.e. it is not fitting for us to compare ourselves with them, i.e. that we should do what they do
with ourselves alone shall we compare ourselves, i.e. as is fitting, we shall not boast of anything that we have not done, as you do, O pseudo-apostles
i.e. the immense; or, it is a measure [?]
i.e. we compare ourselves with ourselves
i.e. he has granted it to us
i.e. in equality with you
i.e. that we are apostles to you
i.e. as though we were not equal with you
i.e. we shall not exalt ourselves too much
i.e. it is not into the fruit of another's preaching that I come
around you on every side
i.e. they will be the same precepts that I would preach to them; or, it is not into the labour of another that I come
i.e. who praises himself
i.e. whom the Lord praises
bear with
i.e. bear with me, i.e. you bear with someone who is worse for you, i.e. the pseudo-apostles
jealousy
i.e. my jealousy and God's for you are the same
i.e. for I have betrothed you
i.e. without thinking of anything else except Christ
i.e. it was to Eve that the serpent came, not to Adam, because woman is weaker than man; so it is no wonder to me, then, that it is the weak among you that he will do it to
i.e. a cutting off [?]
i.e. from me, i.e. whom we have not preached to you
i.e. it would be right for you to believe him in that way, or you would rightly bear with listening to us, if our teaching is not the same [as his]; and if it is not [?] for you, do not listen to us
i.e. by humbling myself, because he who humbles himself will be exalted.
i.e. while I was preaching to them, it was the Macedonians who came to me
i.e. I was not a burden on anyone
i.e. not asking for anything from you
